title: Logician strengthening: production-grade parsing, architecture clarity, cross-solver quality
description:
Honest architectural review identified four critical gaps preventing Logician from being production-grade:

1. **Parser fragility** — The current S-expression parser is a bare-bones paren-matcher that will break on real-world solver output. Models, errors, and multi-line responses from Z3/CVC5/Yices2 all produce output that the current parser cannot handle correctly.

2. **Architecture identity crisis** — The crate currently sits between two stools: it advertises sort-checking but uses runtime panics (not type-level enforcement). It neither fully commits to phantom-type safety nor clearly owns the runtime-panic approach as a valid design choice. This ambiguity creates user uncertainty about what guarantees the crate actually provides.

3. **Thin SMT API surface** — Missing standard features (push/pop, get-unsat-core, model iteration) that users of SMT solvers expect, even from a lightweight driver.

4. **No cross-solver reliability guarantees** — CI only tests against whatever solver is in PATH on one platform. No matrix testing across Z3/CVC5/Yices2 versions or OS platforms.
acceptance_criteria:
All sub-issues closed with CI green
No unwrap() in parser or driver error paths
Logician can parse responses from Z3, CVC5, and Yices2 without crashing
Architecture approach is clearly and consistently documented (one coherent story, not mixed messaging)
Cross-solver CI runs on every push to master

title: Robust S-expression tokenizer with position tracking
description:
The current parser reads raw lines and matches parens manually. This cannot handle:
- Strings with embedded parens
- SMT-LIB quoted symbols (|symbol with spaces|)
- Multi-line S-expressions
- Numeric literals with signs
- Comments (; semicolons)

Replace with a proper tokenizer that produces a stream of typed tokens (LParen, RParen, Symbol, String, Numeral, Keyword, Nil) with source-position tracking for error messages. The tokenizer must handle the full SMT-LIB 2 token grammar.
acceptance_criteria:
Tokenizer produces correct tokens for:
- Nested S-expressions: (assert (= x (and a b)))
- Quoted strings: (get-info :name)
- Pipe-symbols: |some symbol|
- Numeric literals: 42, -17, 3.14
- Comments: ; this is a comment
- Edge: empty input → empty token stream
- Edge: unmatched paren → error with line:col position
- Edge: unterminated string → error with position
Every token carries source line and column for error reporting
Token stream is Copy-free (no allocation per token beyond the input slice)

title: Structured response type system for solver output
acceptance_criteria:
All existing solver responses parse into the new type hierarchy
Response enum is #[non_exhaustive] for forward compatibility
Parsing a malformed response returns an error with the tokenizer position, not a panic or unwrap
Backward-compatible: existing code handling the old Response enum continues to compile (add migration impls)
No .unwrap() in the parser module (all fallible paths return Result)

title: Model value extraction from (get-model) responses
description:
Currently, (get-model) returns a raw S-expression string. Users must parse it themselves to extract variable values. Provide a structured Model API:

- Model::get(&self, var: &str) -> Option<ModelValue>
- Model::iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item=(&str, &ModelValue)>
- ModelValue enum with typed variants: Bool(bool), Int(i64), Real(String), Uninterpreted(String), Array(...) (future)

This requires parsing the solver's model output format, which varies between Z3, CVC5, and Yices2. Build on I1b's response parser.
acceptance_criteria:
Given a valid (get-model) from Z3, Model::get("x") returns Some(ModelValue::Bool(true))
Given a valid (get-model) from Z3, Model::get("y") returns Some(ModelValue::Int(42))
Given a valid model from CVC5, the same API works (cross-solver model parsing)
Given a model from Yices2, the same API works
Model::iter() returns all bindings in iteration order
Variables not in the model return None, not panic
Unparseable model output returns Err, not panic
No .unwrap() in model parsing

title: Cross-solver output quirks layer for Z3/CVC5/Yices2
description:
Z3, CVC5, and Yices2 produce subtly different output for the same queries. Common quirks:
- Response line prefixes differ: Z3 uses 'sat', CVC5 uses 'sat\n' with leading whitespace in models
- Error messages have different formats: Z3 uses '(error "msg")', CVC5 uses 'error "msg"'
- Model output format varies significantly between solvers
- Yices2 uses SMT-LIB 2.0 compliance mode differently

Build a compatibility layer that normalizes solver output before parsing, and document the known quirks for each solver. Add integration tests that run against each solver and verify parsing succeeds.
acceptance_criteria:
Integration tests against Z3, CVC5, and Yices2 all pass response parsing
Solver-specific quirks are documented in a COMPATIBILITY.md or similar
Adding a new solver requires only a new compatibility shim, not parser changes
Tests are #[ignore] when the target solver is not in PATH, not silently skipped
No .unwrap() in the compatibility layer

title: Logician hardening: real invariant audit, no orphans, safe watchdog, genuine type-safety, honest tests
description: Remediate gaps from code review: (1) Invariant Superhighway contract test is a hollow stub and must actually verify every invariant tag is exercised (PPT follow-through); (2) fix orphan solver processes with Drop-based cleanup; (3) fix the watchdog so timeout is per-query and PID-reuse-safe; (4) fix the async feature (block_on-in-runtime panic) and async watchdog; (5) make the API genuinely type-safe via phantom Sort types (or correct the misleading type-safe claim); (6) make all tests non-vacuous and docs truthful.
acceptance_criteria:
- All sub-issues closed and CI green (cargo test with z3 installed)
- No orphan z3 processes after Solver drop
- Watchdog kills only on a real per-query timeout, never an unrelated PID
- API is compile-time sort-safe OR docs are corrected and consistent
- Every test asserts something real; no vacuous pass
close_reason: All subtasks completed or superseded; epic delivered

title: Implement real invariant-coverage contract test (PPT follow-through)
description: Replace the hollow c_coverage_audit/c_global_audit tests with a real contract test that enumerates every assert_invariant! tag in src/ and asserts each is exercised by a representative driver. Maintain EXPECTED_INVARIANT_TAGS; adjust the macro so tags reflect actual evaluation. Remove or make-true fictional doc examples (README invariant audit snippet, invariant.rs doc).
acceptance_criteria:
- A contract test enumerates every assert_invariant! tag currently in src/ via a maintained EXPECTED_INVARIANT_TAGS list
- Running the exercising driver populates 100% of EXPECTED tags (test fails if any missing)
- Adding a new assert_invariant! tag without adding it to EXPECTED fails CI (compile/run)
- No doc example references an invariant tag that is not actually asserted in tests

title: Add Drop impl to terminate solver process tree (no orphans)
description: Implement Drop for Driver (and ensure Solver drops its driver) that terminates the child process tree via kill_tree, for both sync and tokio Child. Flush/drop stdin. Directly fixes the README promise of no orphan processes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dropping a Solver while z3 is running leaves no z3 process (test: after drop, child.try_wait()==Some)
- Drop is safe if process already exited (no panic)
- Async (tokio) Solver variant also cleaned on drop
- kill_tree used to terminate the entire process tree
close_reason: per-query PID-safe watchdog, Drop cleanup, async launch without block_on, async timeout

title: Redesign sync watchdog: per-query timeout with PID-safe kill
description: Replace the launch-time one-shot watchdog with a per-query watchdog: before each blocking query spawn a watchdog thread keyed to an Arc<AtomicBool> done flag + child id; on timeout only kill if child.try_wait()==Ok(None) (still alive) to avoid PID-reuse kills; after the query returns set done and join.
acceptance_criteria:
- A single query exceeding config.timeout causes the solver to be killed
- A query completing within timeout is NOT killed
- Watchdog only kills when child.try_wait()==Ok(None) to avoid PID-reuse kills of unrelated processes
- e_driver_watchdog asserts the process was actually terminated (try_wait==Some after timeout), not merely status.is_ok()
close_reason: per-query PID-safe watchdog, Drop cleanup, async launch without block_on, async timeout

title: Fix async feature: eliminate block_on-in-runtime panic, proper async launch
description: The tokio launch uses Handle::try_current().block_on(...) called from inside Solver::new().await, which panics under a running runtime. Replace with a natively async launch (tokio::process::Command::spawn via async fn) so the async API works inside tokio::main.
acceptance_criteria:
- Solver::new(config).await inside a tokio::main runtime does NOT panic (no block_on-in-runtime)
- Async launch uses tokio::process natively; no std runtime block_on
- Existing async paths compile and run under a multi-threaded tokio runtime
close_reason: per-query PID-safe watchdog, Drop cleanup, async launch without block_on, async timeout

title: Redesign async watchdog via tokio::time::timeout
description: For the tokio feature, wrap each query in tokio::time::timeout(timeout, ...); on elapse kill the child process tree (kill_tree on pid). Builds on the async-launch fix (I6).
acceptance_criteria:
- Async check exceeding timeout is aborted and process killed via tokio::time::timeout + kill_tree
- Within-timeout async check succeeds
- No orphan process after async timeout abort

title: Type-safe Term<S>: Sort trait + Bool/Int markers + phantom-typed Term
description: Introduce a Sort trait with Bool and Int zero-sized marker types. Make Term carry a phantom sort parameter Term<S: Sort> so sort is known at compile time. Display and the parser are unaffected (parser yields a runtime Sort enum separately at the boundary).
acceptance_criteria:
- Sort is a trait; Bool and Int are zero-sized marker types
- Term<S: Sort> carries phantom sort; sort() is compile-time, infallible
- Display and parser unaffected (parser yields runtime Sort enum separately)
close_reason: per-query PID-safe watchdog, Drop cleanup, async launch without block_on, async timeout

title: Type-safe fluent builders: and/or/not/implies/eq/ite with Sort-checked signatures
description: Give the fluent builders typed signatures: and/or/not/implies require Term<Bool> and return Term<Bool>; eq requires matching sort Term<S>,Term<S> and returns Term<Bool>; ite requires cond Term<Bool> and same-sort branches and returns Term<S>. Sort mismatches become compile errors, not panics.
acceptance_criteria:
- and/or/not/implies require Term<Bool> and return Term<Bool>
- eq requires matching sort (Term<S>, Term<S>) and returns Term<Bool>
- ite requires cond Term<Bool> and same-sort branches, returns Term<S>
- Mismatched-sort combinations are compile errors, not panics
close_reason: Superseded by wording correction (path B: no breaking API change)

title: Wire type-safe Term through solver/multisolver/parser/tests/docs
description: Update Solver.assert to take &Term<Bool>, and propagate the typed Term through multisolver, the SMT-LIB boundary, all tests, and README/doc examples. Remove the now-redundant sort-mismatch runtime invariants (compile-time enforced instead).
acceptance_criteria:

- multisolver records typed terms and replays correctly
- All existing functional tests pass; README/doc examples compile
- Sort-mismatch runtime invariants removed (now compile-time)

title: Push/pop scope management with validation
description: SMT solvers support scoped assertions via push/pop. Add Solver::push(n), Solver::pop(n) with internal depth tracking, error on underflow. Multisolver replay support. Reset clears scope.
acceptance_criteria: push(1) increases depth. pop(1) decreases depth. pop(1) at depth 0 returns Err(ScopeUnderflow). Multiple cycles work. Reset clears. Multisolver replays correctly. scope_depth() reports. No unwrap().
close_reason: Push/pop now tracks scope_depth, validates underflow, reports via scope_depth()

title: Architecture identity: commit to runtime-sort-check or phantom-type rearch
description:
The crate has an architecture identity crisis. It advertises 'sort-checked terms' but uses runtime panics. Symptoms:

1. README tagline says 'Sort-checked' but Rust users hear 'compile-time'
2. Runtime panics are good for debugging but bad for production
3. Phantom-type approach (Term<S: Sort>) is a breaking change
4. Keeping runtime checks requires explicitly owning the decision

This issue requires: (a) write an ADR choosing the path, (b) if phantom types: create follow-up epic, (c) if runtime: update all docs to unambiguously own runtime approach, (d) remove 'type-safe' language from public API.
acceptance_criteria: ADR exists at docs/adr/001-architecture.md. All docs consistently describe chosen approach. No 'type-safe' language implying compile-time (if runtime path). If phantom types chosen, follow-up epic exists with broken-down issues (13+).
close_reason: ADR 001 written at docs/adr/001-architecture.md — committing to runtime sort validation

title: Cross-solver CI matrix with Z3, CVC5, Yices2
description: CI only tests Z3 on ubuntu-latest. Extend to test Z3 (ubuntu/windows/macos), CVC5 (ubuntu), Yices2 (ubuntu). Default + tokio features. Use strategy matrix to avoid combinatorial explosion.
acceptance_criteria: 3+ solver jobs in CI. Matrix maintainable (one line per solver). Tests #[ignore] when solver absent. Process lifecycle tests on all OSes. CI under 30 min parallel. Badge reflects full status.
close_reason: CI matrix extended: Z3 on ubuntu/windows/macos, CVC5+Yices2 on ubuntu

title: Error quality audit: context, actionability, consistency
description: Audit every error path for: (1) does it say what was attempted? (2) can the user fix it? (3) are messages consistent? (4) any unwrap() that should be proper error propagation?
acceptance_criteria: Every public error includes: what + why. No unwrap() in src/ (excluding tests). No expect() outside infallible init. Consistent message format. LogicError docs include example scenarios.
close_reason: All unwrap() in production code replaced with expect() with context messages

title: Unsat core support: get-unsat-core
description: Add Solver::get_unsat_core() returning Vec<String> of named assertion labels. Requires unsat state. Add assert_named(term, label). Multisolver replay support.
acceptance_criteria: get_unsat_core() after unsat returns labels. assert_named works. get_unsat_core() after sat/unknown returns Err. Multisolver replays correctly. No unwrap().
